test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 30 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Who among the following extends the jurisdiction of a High Court to, or excludes it from, any union territory?

options.text: Legislature of the State in which the High Court is situated

solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament by Law**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Parliament of India can** extend or exclude a** High Court's jurisdiction over a Union Territory. **This is done by passing a law. 
 
• The jurisdiction of a High Court **is normally limited to the state it is located in and the Union Territory it is associated with.** 
 
• The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 extended the jurisdiction of High Courts to Union Territories. 
 
• Example
 
 
• The **Madras High Court **has jurisdiction over the state of Tamil Nadu and the Union Territory of Puducherry. 
 
• The **Kerala High Court **has jurisdiction over the state of Kerala and the Union Territory of Lakshadweep.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Articles 214 to 231 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the organisation, independence, jurisdiction, powers, procedures and so on of the high courts.
 
• The judiciary in a state consists of a high court and a hierarchy of subordinate courts. The high court occupies the top position in the judicial administration of a state.

History

 
• The institution of high court originated in India in 1862 when the high courts were set up at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.
 
• In 1866, a fourth high court was established at Allahabad. In the course of time, each province in British India came to have its own high court.
 
• After 1950, a high court existing in a province became the high court for the corresponding state.
